Empty `worksheets` for a household with no US person — not a 404. "Nobody here files"

post.description: Assemble a PlanInput from the database and run the projection.

schema.title: Response Run Projection Api Project Post

post.description:
Solve for the monthly spending/contribution that hits a goal.

Bisects the pure projection ("solve for X", die-with-zero).

Solve for a retirement date, or report the odds of one.

The answer deliberately differs from `fire.fi_dates`: that is net worth crossing the
4%-rule `fire_number`, this is the simulated date with AOW timing, pension unlock and
Box 3 drag in play. Both travel back so the UI can show them side by side.
Sweep the knob and return the spending-vs-success curve.
Rank the assumptions by how far each one moves the metric (the tornado).

get.description: Return one household and everything hanging off it as a single JSON document.

schema.title: Response Export Household Api Export Get

post.description:
Load a whole household from an export document.

Ids are preserved verbatim, which keeps every foreign key valid without remapping —
including the ones buried in milestone `params` and scenario `overrides` dict-keys.
That makes the target an *empty* database: the browser build opens one each session
and a restore starts clean, so a colliding id is refused with 409 rather than merged.
NOTE: preserve-ids-into-empty-DB. Merging into a populated database would mean
remapping every id (and rewriting those embedded references) — the reason it 409s.

schema.title: Response Import Household Api Import Post

delete.description:
Delete one household and every row that hangs off it, leaving import a clean target.

The plain household DELETE refuses while people or accounts still reference it. This
is the way out of the example household: start empty, or import a saved export.
Dependants go first, in the reverse of import's insert order, for the FK checks.

get.description:
Return the resolved tax config for a year, per field with its provenance.

This is the tax panel's read model. A scenario_id resolves through that scenario's
tax overrides, so overridden fields come back with status "user".

schema.title: Response Get Tax Config Api Tax Config Get

get.description:
What a first-time reader needs in order to judge the numbers in front of them.

Two facts that belong together because they answer the same question — "how much
should I trust this?" — and nothing on the Plan surface was saying either. Whose
numbers these are was marked only in the browser build, and what the model does not
cover was written down only in the regime modules' docstrings.

ExtraRepayment-Input.title: ExtraRepayment
ExtraRepayment-Input.description:
Milestone params: pay `monthly_amount` extra into the mortgage, every month.

The aflossen half of aflossen-vs-beleggen. It runs from the milestone
date until the mortgage is gone; the annuity payment is *not* recalculated, so the
term shortens rather than the monthly payment dropping — "looptijd verkorten", not
"maandlast verlagen". The other choice is not modelled: re-amortising would lower the
payment and save less interest, so this models the variant that favours repaying.

FbarRequest.title: FbarRequest
FbarRequest.description:
A projection request plus the reporting year to read off it.

Subclasses `ProjectRequest` rather than repeating it: the worksheet is a *reading* of
a projection, so it must be built from the same plan, the same assumptions and the
same start date the user is looking at. Monte Carlo fields are inherited and ignored —
a filing obligation is not a distribution, so run 0 is what gets read.

RetirementRequest.title: RetirementRequest
RetirementRequest.description:
Request body for /api/retirement — early retirement, both directions.

Exactly one of `at_date` / `probability`: the first reports the odds for a date the
user names, the second solves for the earliest date clearing a probability they name.
Sending both is a caller error rather than a silently-picked default.

Shaped like `SolveRequest` rather than `ProjectRequest`: `mode` and
`min_end_net_worth` mean nothing here, and the run count is the only knob wanted.
